confirmed.title: 0% deposit booking made within ~2h of start is confirmed, then forfeited on the next automation tick
confirmed.problem: noDepositDue makes the session status 'confirmed' with nothing paid. automation step 4 cancels any public confirmed session that is not fully paid once now >= start - 2h. createBooking has no minimum lead time; it only requires startTime > now. The client is told 'booked... pay the balance at least 2 hours before it starts', which is impossible. Within 15 minutes they get 'Booking cancelled' and the slot goes to the waitlist. Before this change the 60-minute tentative hold let them pay in full.
confirmed.trigger: A room with depositPct 0 and rateCents > 0. A client books at 1:00pm for a 2:30pm start. The next booking-automation cron sees status confirmed, paid 0, inside 2h. confirmed.fix: In createBooking, take the noDepositDue path only when args.startTime - Date.now() > 2*HOUR plus a margin of at least one cron interval (15 min). Otherwise treat the booking as pay-in-full: set depositCents = rateCents (rateCents > 0), keep status 'tentative' with holdExpiresAt, and send the 'Pay $X within 60 minutes' hold message. Add a test for a 0% booking made under 2h before its start.

confirmed.title: Waitlist entry left 'waiting' gets every new freed slot, and finalize may mark the wrong entry
confirmed.problem: proposeWaitlistFill no longer marks the winner, and dedupe is per freed session. Until the owner approves, each further cancellation proposes the same client again, and the next-best waitlisted client is never offered. Previously the second slot went to the next person. finalize marks 'the first waiting entry whose artist email matches'. When a client has two waiting entries (e.g. two rooms), or two artist rows share the email, the entry marked may not be the one that was offered. The offered entry stays waiting and is offered again.

Two proposals go to the same client and approving both sends two 'you get first pick' emails. Or a client has waitlist entries for Room A and Room B: a Room B offer marks the Room A entry notified.
confirmed.fix: Add an optional waitlistEntryId to the waitlist_fill payload (validator included), set it to winner._id in proposeWaitlistFill, and in finalize patch exactly that id (keep the email match only as a fallback for old actions). In proposeWaitlistFill, exclude entries already named by an open (proposed or approved) waitlist_fill action.

confirmed.title: All-day outside-calendar events now block the wrong hours for client bookings
confirmed.problem: roomBusyIntervals now treats every stored externalCalendarEvents row as busy. parseIcal (convex/externalCalendarsActions.ts:82-85) stores ev.start/ev.end exactly as node-ical returns them. For VALUE=DATE (all-day) events node-ical builds `new Date(y, m, d)` in the server's local zone, which is UTC on Convex. An all-day block therefore covers UTC midnight to UTC midnight, not the studio's own day. Before this branch those rows only showed on the staff grid. Now they block both public and staff bookings, 5 to 8 hours off for US studios.
confirmed.trigger: A Los Angeles studio's Apple/Outlook feed has an all-day 'Closed' event on Dec 5. Pulse blocks Dec 4 4pm to Dec 5 4pm PT. A client can book Dec 5 from 6pm to 10pm, and nobody can book the afternoon of Dec 4.
confirmed.fix: In parseIcal, when datetype === 'date', take the calendar date from ev.start (and ev.end) with getUTCFullYear/getUTCMonth/getUTCDate and store midnight-to-midnight in the org's time zone. Pass the org tz into syncFeed, or look it up in upsertEvents. The other option is to keep storing the date key with allDay and have roomBusyIntervals expand it in the org's zone.
confirmed.reviewerFix: In parseIcal, when datetype === 'date', rebuild start and end from the date parts (getUTCFullYear/Month/Date) as midnight in the studio's time zone (orgTz) before storing. Or store allDay with the date key and have roomBusy expand it in the org's zone.

For a VALUE=DATE event, node-ical 0.26.1 (ical.js:356, 842) builds `new Date(y, m-1, d)` in the process's local zone, which is UTC in a Convex Node action. roomBusy.ts:96-108 now pushes every event on an active feed as kind 'calendar' and never reads e.allDay. roomConflict and conflictMessage turn that into a refusal on the public page, in createBooking (booking.ts:841) and in staff create/reschedule (roomStatus.ts:128-136). confirmed.title: A Pulse booking pushed to Google comes back through an .ics feed and blocks its own reschedule and its freed slot
confirmed.problem: The Google pull path skips events Pulse created (googleBusyBlocks). The .ics path has no such skip. When a studio pushes bookings to Google (two_way or push) and also adds that Google calendar's private .ics URL to a room, which add() encourages by detecting 'google', every Pulse session comes back as an externalCalendarEvents row. roomConflict's excludeSessionId does not exclude this copy, and roomStatus throws for any conflict whose kind is not 'session'. When a session is cancelled, its copy keeps blocking the slot until the feed is next refreshed. That can take hours (25 feeds per 30 minutes, plus Google's own .ics lag).
confirmed.trigger: Studio has Google two-way sync and Room A's feed is the same Google calendar. Staff extend a 2-5pm session to 2-6pm: the reschedule throws 'The studio is unavailable at that time.' because the 2-5pm copy overlaps. A client cancels a 2-5pm booking: the waitlist offer goes out, but the slot stays unavailable on the booking page until the feed refreshes.
confirmed.fix: In roomBusyIntervals, drop calendar events whose externalUid, with the '@google.com' suffix stripped, equals a session's googleCalendarEventId or pulseEventId(sessionId). A simpler option is to skip feed events in that org whose uid starts with the Pulse event-id prefix. At minimum, skip the copy belonging to excludeSessionId.
confirmed.reviewerFix: In roomBusyIntervals, drop calendar events whose externalUid matches a session's googleCalendarEventId (Google .ics UIDs are '<eventId>@google.com'). At minimum, drop the copy of excludeSessionId. Or skip events carrying the marker Pulse puts on events it pushes.
confirmed.skepticReason: The Google pull path skips Pulse-origin events (googleCalendarSync.ts:78, PULSE_ORIGIN_TAG). The .ics path has no such skip, and Google's .ics export does not carry private extendedProperties. A studio that pushes to Google and also adds that same calendar's private .ics URL to a room gets a 'calendar' copy of each session. roomConflict's excludeSessionId only filters sessions (roomBusy.ts:72). roomStatus.ts:136 throws for any non-session conflict, so extending or moving that session fails, and a cancelled session's slot stays blocked until the next feed refresh. confirmed.title: The studio health score now loads on every home screen, using a query that reads seven entire tables
confirmed.problem: The new 'health' widget is on by default. It runs api.agentHealth.studioHealth, which calls studioHealthFor (convex/agentHealth.ts:21-27). That function reads every payment, invoice, session, room, opportunity, song and artist the studio has ever had, with no limit. Before this change the panel was only on the Growth-only /agent page. Now the query runs reactively for every member with insights.read on every dashboard load, and it re-runs on any change to any of those tables. Once a studio's history passes Convex's per-query read limit (16,384 documents or 8 MB), the query throws. The dashboard widgets have no error boundary, so the throw takes down the whole (app) route and shows src/app/(app)/error.tsx in place of the home screen.
confirmed.trigger: A studio about two years in, with roughly 6k sessions, 6k invoices and 6k payments, opens /dashboard. studioHealth reads more than 16k documents, throws, and the home screen shows the error page for everyone in that studio.

Real fix: bound studioHealthFor the way dashboard.ts does. Use `.gte("_creationTime", now - 90*DAY)` index ranges, or `.take(N)`, for payments, invoices, sessions and opportunities.
